courseTitle: Microsoft Data & BI Capstone + Job Preparation

lessons.title: Architecture Planning: Raw Data to Reporting

slots.practicalActivity: Watch the kickoff and architecture-planning lessons, then draw your own end-to-end architecture diagram for the capstone: raw source -> SQL Server staging -> SSIS ETL -> warehouse facts/dimensions -> SSRS report + Power BI dashboard. Label each box with the earlier LTV Academy course it reuses (SQL Server, SSIS, Data Warehousing, SSRS, Power BI), and name the real database and table names you will actually build in the next several hours.
slots.deliverable: A hand-drawn or diagrammed capstone architecture map with each stage labeled to its source course, plus a written list of the exact database/table names you'll build.

lessons.title: Loading Raw Data With SQL Server

slots.practicalActivity: In SQL Server Management Studio, create a new database for your capstone project and build the raw/source tables shown in the lesson. Load them with real sample rows using T-SQL INSERT statements (or a flat-file import), using the exact CREATE TABLE and data-loading syntax taught in the SQL Server Database Development course — no new techniques.
slots.deliverable: A running SQL Server database with raw tables populated with real rows, confirmed with a SELECT * query that returns your loaded data.

slots.practicalActivity: In SQL Server Data Tools, build your own SSIS package with a Data Flow Task that extracts rows from the raw tables you created last hour, applies at least one transformation (Derived Column or Data Conversion), and loads the result into a new staging table — reusing the same control-flow and data-flow patterns from the SSIS course.
slots.deliverable: A working .dtsx SSIS package that executes successfully end to end and populates your staging table with transformed rows.

slots.practicalActivity: Design and create your warehouse schema (kept separate from staging) with T-SQL CREATE TABLE statements, following the staging-to-warehouse separation pattern from the Data Warehousing course. Confirm the staging tables from last hour still load correctly into this new structure.
slots.deliverable: An empty but correctly structured warehouse schema, with a written note confirming the staging-to-warehouse data path is ready.

slots.practicalActivity: Build at least one dimension table (e.g., a Date dimension) and one fact table for your capstone data, populating both from your staging tables with T-SQL INSERT...SELECT statements, applying the star-schema modeling rules from the Data Warehousing course.
slots.deliverable: Populated fact and dimension tables in your warehouse, verified with a join query that returns correctly aggregated results.

slots.practicalActivity: In Report Builder, build a paginated report against your warehouse tables, including at least one grouped table or matrix and one report parameter, reusing the dataset design and layout techniques from the SSRS course.
slots.deliverable: A deployed SSRS paginated report (.rdl) that renders real rows pulled live from your warehouse tables.

slots.practicalActivity: In Power BI Desktop, connect to your warehouse tables, build a data model relating your fact and dimension tables, and create a dashboard with at least three visuals (a KPI card, a chart, and a slicer), reusing the modeling and DAX techniques from the Power BI course.
slots.deliverable: A Power BI (.pbix) dashboard with at least 3 working visuals connected live to your warehouse tables.

lessons.title: Connecting SSRS & Power BI to the Same Warehouse

slots.practicalActivity: Point your SSRS report's dataset and your Power BI dashboard's data source at the exact same warehouse connection. Change one fact row's value directly in the warehouse, then refresh both tools and confirm the new number appears correctly in both.
slots.deliverable: A short written note (or screenshot pair) showing the same updated number appearing in both the SSRS report and the Power BI dashboard after one shared-warehouse change.

lessons.title: Validating the Full Pipeline, End to End

slots.practicalActivity: Run your full pipeline from scratch: re-execute the SSIS package, confirm the warehouse repopulates, then refresh the SSRS report and Power BI dashboard. Record the row count at every stage (raw -> staging -> warehouse -> report/dashboard) to confirm nothing was lost or duplicated anywhere.
slots.deliverable: A written validation log listing row counts at each of the four pipeline stages, confirming end-to-end correctness.

slots.practicalActivity: Simulate a late schema change: add one new column to a raw source table (e.g., a Region field). Update your SSIS package, warehouse table, SSRS report, and Power BI dashboard so the new column flows correctly through the entire pipeline without breaking anything already built.
slots.deliverable: An updated pipeline (SSIS package + warehouse table + SSRS report + Power BI dashboard) that successfully surfaces the new column end to end.

lessons.title: Deployment Across SSIS, SSRS & Power BI

slots.practicalActivity: Deploy your SSIS package to the SSIS Catalog, publish your SSRS report to a report server, and publish your Power BI dashboard to the Power BI service. Then configure a SQL Server Agent job (or Power BI scheduled refresh) to run your SSIS package and refresh your dashboard automatically on a daily schedule.
slots.deliverable: A deployed, scheduled version of your full capstone pipeline, with a screenshot of the configured job/schedule.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-to-two-page solution document for your capstone covering the architecture, table list, and refresh schedule. Then check the SSIS Catalog's execution reports (or SQL Server Agent job history) for your last scheduled run and write down whether it succeeded, and what you'd look at first if it had failed.
slots.deliverable: A written solution document, plus a screenshot of a job execution log and a short note on how you'd diagnose a failure.

lessons.title: Building Your Resume Around This Project

slots.practicalActivity: Write an actual resume bullet-point section describing your capstone project: tools used (SQL Server, SSIS, SSRS, Power BI), what you built, and one measurable outcome. Then outline a 5-minute portfolio presentation script you would give a hiring manager, walking through your warehouse, report, and dashboard in order.
slots.deliverable: A real resume draft section for the capstone project, plus a written 5-minute portfolio presentation outline.

lessons.title: Common Microsoft BI Developer Interview Questions

slots.practicalActivity: Push your SSIS project files, .rdl report, and .pbix dashboard (or a documented export of each) to a GitHub repository with a README describing the capstone project. Then write your own answers to 3 real Microsoft BI developer interview questions from the lesson, in your own words.
slots.deliverable: A GitHub repository containing your capstone project files and README, plus 3 written interview-question answers.

slots.practicalActivity: Do a mock technical walkthrough out loud (recorded, or with a study partner) explaining your capstone's SQL Server -> SSIS -> warehouse -> SSRS/Power BI pipeline as if presenting to an interviewer. Then write one STAR-format answer (Situation, Task, Action, Result) to a behavioral question like 'Tell me about a time you solved a data problem,' using your late-schema-change fix from earlier as the real example.
slots.deliverable: A written STAR-format behavioral answer, plus notes (or a recording) from your mock technical walkthrough.

lessons.title: Where to Go Next: An Overview of Advanced Tracks

slots.practicalActivity: Find 3 real Microsoft BI Developer job postings online and write down the listed salary range and required skills for each. Draft one sentence you would actually say if negotiating an offer. Then write down which advanced track from the lesson (e.g., Data Engineering, Databricks, Snowflake/dbt) you personally want to study next.
slots.deliverable: Written notes on 3 real job postings with salary ranges, a drafted negotiation sentence, and your personal choice of next advanced track.

slots.practicalActivity: Deliver your full capstone presentation end to end (recorded or live to a friend/mentor): the business scenario, the architecture, a live demo of your SSRS report and Power BI dashboard, and the late-schema-change story as your 'how I handled a real problem' moment. Then write a half-page reflection on the full 6-month program: what you built, what you're proudest of, and your first concrete job-search action for next week.
slots.deliverable: A recorded or witnessed end-to-end capstone presentation, plus a written half-page program reflection with one concrete next action.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: Can present a real, self-built, end-to-end Microsoft BI pipeline (SQL Server through SSIS, a warehouse, SSRS, and Power BI) with a resume, GitHub portfolio, and practiced interview answers ready — completing the full 6-month Microsoft Data & BI Developer program and ready to apply for junior BI developer roles.
